clue.text: Deal in motor vehicles

definitions.meaning: to deal in goods, often illicit ones, is to trade in them
the cars and lorries moving along the roads, taken collectively

explanation.surface: Someone runs a business buying and selling cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal in' reads as one phrase for selling cars, but 'in' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for illegal trading and a noun for the flow of cars on a road.

clue.text: Roof yonder church

parts.note: that, as in that one over there

explanation.surface: A distant church's roof is in view.
explanation.definitionFit: A covering of straw or reeds forms a traditional roof on cottages.

clue.text: Look for a soft fruit

parts.note: P, piano, the musical direction for soft
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone searches for a squashy fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look for' reads as searching, but 'Look' is the definition (seem) and 'for' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To look a certain way is to seem or give that impression.

clue.text: Panic over draw? Nonsense!

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a flap is a state of panic
to doodle is to draw idly

explanation.surface: Someone frets about a tied match and is told not to be silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' suggests a tied game but means sketching; 'over' puts FLAP above DOODLE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for foolish talk, a synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Arrived and left by desert transport

parts.note: came means arrived

explanation.surface: Someone turns up and departs on a beast of the sands.
explanation.definitionFit: The humped animal is the classic means of crossing the Sahara.

clue.text: One politician everyone wants to indict

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
MP, Member of Parliament
each, as in every single one

explanation.surface: A lone politician is the target of universal calls for prosecution.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a public official formally with misconduct is a synonym for indicting them.

clue.text: Usually where water is found

definitions.meaning: an idiom for generally or for the most part
inside the water pipe that supplies a street

explanation.surface: Water can normally be found in a particular place.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means for the most part, and literally names the place inside the water main, the large supply pipe under a street.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means generally, and literally places water inside the large supply pipe under the road.

clue.text: Keep returning to take a look

indicators.note: the word keep comes back on itself, read from the end

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going back for a glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' tells you to read KEEP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick, sly glance is a synonym for taking a look.

clue.text: Guaranteed to get a Tory leader put on trial

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: tested means put on trial, tried out

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief is certain to end up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on trial' suggests a court case but means tried out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vouched for formally, as by a witness, is certified or guaranteed.

clue.text: Really snug home in divine setting

indicators.note: the cosy home goes inside the word for divine
the word for divine forms a setting around the cosy home

parts.note: holy means divine
a nest is a cosy home

explanation.surface: A cosy house set in heavenly surroundings is truly wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snug home' is one piece, a bird's nest; 'in' and 'setting' together signal the container.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation it means truly or in truth, a synonym for really.

clue.text: Top mark in final Pharmacy exam

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words final Pharmacy, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A student earns the best grade in the last pharmacy examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' tells you the answer is hidden: finAL PHArmacy.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Greek letter is used as the highest grade a marker can award, as in alpha plus.

clue.text: The one mat ruined by insect infestation

definitions.text: The one mat ruined by insect infestation

indicators.note: the words the one mat are wrecked, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A single rug has been spoilt by bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' signals rearranging THEONEMAT; the whole clue also describes the answer, since a mat chewed by grubs is exactly what the word means.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes fabric holed by the larvae of clothes-eating moths.

clue.text: Ned and Charlie used it to shed light

definitions.text: Ned and Charlie used it to shed light

indicators.note: the names Ned and Charlie are put to use in a new order, their letters reworked

explanation.surface: Two men relied on a fitting to illuminate a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' signals rearranging the letters of NED and CHARLIE, leaving out 'and'; the whole clue doubles as a description of a hanging light fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative hanging fitting with branches holding many lamps or candles is a source of light.

clue.text: Divine lady currently in Oxford

definitions.meaning: an Egyptian goddess, wife of Osiris
the name of the river Thames as its current flows through Oxford

explanation.surface: A holy woman is presently living in a university city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currently' looks like 'at present' but means 'as a current of water': the Thames is called the Isis where it passes through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: One name serves both an ancient Egyptian mother goddess and the stretch of the Thames at Oxford.

clue.text: Create a religion? Sheer fantasy!

parts.note: to make is to create
a belief, a faith

explanation.surface: Inventing a faith is pure imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant of make-believe, the pretending of a child at play, so pure imagination.

clue.text: Ring in perfect condition

definitions.meaning: a bell rings, so to ring is to make the noise of a bell
an idiom for completely healthy or undamaged

explanation.surface: A ring is found to be flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' tempts as the jewellery of the surface, but it is the verb: what a struck bell does.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in excellent health or working order, and read literally describes the noise of a ringing bell.

clue.text: Cloth recently produced in America

definitions.note: a place in the United States, a state

parts.note: new means recently produced
jersey is a knitted cloth

explanation.surface: Fabric has just been made in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the reverse order to the clue; 'in America' defines a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: The state on the eastern seaboard between New York and Pennsylvania is one of the fifty in the USA.

clue.text: Father consumed large fish

indicators.note: the word for father swallows the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a founder is a father of an institution, as in the founding fathers

explanation.surface: A dad ate a big fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' tempts as FR or PA, but it is FOUNDER, which 'consumed' wraps around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish such as the plaice family includes this species.

clue.text: They don't believe this tea's freshly brewed

indicators.note: a new brew of the words this tea's, their letters stirred up

explanation.surface: Unbelievers are judged by a pot of tea just made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freshly brewed' rearranges THISTEAS; the 's here is 'is', so its S counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonbelievers deny that any god exists, so they lack religious faith.

clue.text: Child prodigy? One might have guessed!

definitions.meaning: a young marvel, a small person who amazes
said when something is unsurprising, an idiom for no surprise

explanation.surface: A gifted youngster turns out exactly as everyone expected.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom meaning it is no surprise, and read literally it describes a small marvel, hence the prodigy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gifted youngster is a small marvel, while the idiom says something is hardly surprising.

clue.text: Snobbish boy and girl

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Ida, a girl's name

explanation.surface: A boy and girl are stuck-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for pretentious or affectedly genteel, so superior.

clue.text: People of standing have good access

parts.note: entry means access

explanation.surface: Important people get good admission.
explanation.definitionFit: The class just below the nobility, well-born landowners, are people of rank.

clue.text: Heartless attendant who exploits others

indicators.note: the middle letter, the heart of the word, is removed

parts.note: an usher is an attendant who shows people to their seats

explanation.surface: A cruel attendant takes advantage of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who manipulates others for gain is called this, as in a selfish person who exploits friends.

clue.text: Consider how to bring journalist back free

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the journalist is turned to face backwards

parts.note: ED, short for editor, the crossword journalist
to liberate is to set free

explanation.surface: Someone ponders how to secure a reporter's release.
explanation.walkthrough: ED, for editor, is the stock crossword journalist; 'back' is the reversal signal, while 'how to bring' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to weigh something up carefully, a synonym for considering it.

clue.text: Tenant found for small place offshore

definitions.meaning: split into two words, a tenant has been found when the property is rented out
a little island near the coast

explanation.surface: A renter is located for a tiny island.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IS LET, the answer says a tenant has been found; 'for' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny isle near the coast, and read as two words it says a property has been rented.

clue.text: One medic under 50 is a member

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces sit under the first

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
the Roman numeral for one
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor in their fifties is a club member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts I and MB below L in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is a member of the body.

clue.text: One Sunday School in gloomy setting gets the chop

indicators.note: the first group goes inside the word for gloomy
the word for gloomy acts as a setting around the letters, holding them like a jewel

parts.note: dismal means gloomy
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Sunday School teacher is sacked in depressing circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One', 'Sunday' and 'School' each give a single letter; 'in' and 'setting' together signal the container, 'the chop' being slang for the sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the chop is slang for being sacked from a job.

clue.text: Moron gets Amin to make a comeback

parts.note: Idi Amin, the Ugandan dictator, so his first name

indicators.note: the word to comes back, read from right to left

explanation.surface: A fool lets a deposed dictator return to power.
explanation.walkthrough: Amin is the Ugandan dictator, whose first name is wanted; 'make a comeback' is the reversal signal for 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are insults for a very stupid person, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Rex, Sybil and I dressed ludicrously

parts.note: R, abbreviation of rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: the letters are dressed up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Three people wore absurd costumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' rearranges R, SYBIL and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something laughably is a synonym for doing it in a ridiculous way.

clue.text: Material from Much Ado About Nothing and What you will

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel, a fuss over nothing
any, as in whatever you like

explanation.surface: Fabric is sourced from two Shakespeare comedies.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Shakespeare titles (the second is Twelfth Night's subtitle) are not plays here: a squabble over nothing is a TIFF, and 'what you will' means ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin gauze muslin fabric bears this name, so it is a kind of material.
